tasks.title: Digital Study Tools and Learner Responsibility
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts in 240–280 words. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.text: Digital study tools such as adaptive learning platforms and AI-driven tutors are often praised for their ability to personalise education and close achievement gaps. By tailoring content to individual pace and providing instant feedback, these tools can make learning more efficient and accessible, especially for students who lack traditional support. However, the convenience they offer comes with a hidden cost: the data generated by every click and response is harvested, analysed, and often monetised by private companies. Students may be unaware that their learning patterns, weaknesses, and even emotional states are being tracked. The promise of personalised learning thus masks a troubling trade-off: in exchange for convenience, learners surrender control over their personal data, and the long-term consequences for privacy and autonomy remain largely unregulated.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.text: Critics of data-driven education overlook a crucial point: the collection of learning data is not inherently exploitative. When governed transparently and ethically, such data can empower students and educators alike. For instance, anonymised analytics can reveal systemic inequities in curriculum design or highlight effective teaching strategies that benefit entire cohorts. Moreover, the argument that students are passive victims of data extraction underestimates their agency. Many young people are digitally literate and capable of making informed choices about the tools they use. The real responsibility lies not with technology itself but with institutions that fail to educate students about data rights and fail to enforce robust ethical standards. To reject digital study tools outright is to ignore their potential to democratise education, particularly for learners in under-resourced settings.

tasks.title: Review of a Digital Study Tool
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: A specialist magazine for educators is running a series of reviews of digital study tools that claim to personalise learning. You decide to write a review of a digital study tool you have used (for example, an adaptive quiz app, a language-learning platform, or an AI essay checker). In your review, evaluate how effectively the tool balances personalised support with respect for user data and learner autonomy. Describe one specific feature that you found either empowering or concerning, and recommend whether other educators should adopt the tool in their teaching context.

tasks.title: Report on Data Governance in Digital Study Tools
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: You are a consultant hired by a regional education authority. The programme coordinator has asked you to write a report on how schools in the region are currently managing the data generated by digital study tools. In your report, analyse the main risks to student privacy and autonomy arising from current practices, assess the potential consequences for trust in educational institutions if these risks are not addressed, and propose two concrete actions that the authority could take to ensure responsible data governance while preserving the benefits of digital tools.

tasks.title: Article: Should Learners Worry About Data Privacy?
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: An English-language online magazine for international readers is publishing a series on 'Learning in the Digital Age'. The editors have invited readers to submit articles addressing the question: Should learners be concerned about the data collected by digital study tools, or is the convenience worth the risk? In your article, explain your position on this issue, discuss one practical consequence of your view for how students choose and use digital tools, and suggest how educational institutions could help learners make informed decisions.
